# Zod Q-lite three-repeat comparison — 2026-08-24

## Verdict

Q-lite is **not an accuracy improvement**. The raw preregistered comparison
scored 0/6 for the full controller (`Q`) and 0/6 for Q-lite (`R`). A post-run
ground-truth audit then found that the `zod-5937` issue-only controller contract
was invalid for both arms: the authentic source fix intentionally changes two
expectations in the prescribed pre-fix `partial` and input-JSON-Schema suites.
The correct fix therefore cannot satisfy the controller as written.

That invalidates the two-cluster efficacy comparison rather than turning six
`zod-5937` failures into evidence against either arm. The remaining valid task
cluster, `zod-5917`, was a 0/3 tie:

| valid task | arm | source accuracy | protocol resolved | median turns | median reminders |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `zod-5917` | full Q (8 obligations) | 0/3 | 3/3 | 38 | 2 |
| `zod-5917` | Q-lite (3 obligations) | 0/3 | 3/3 | 43 | 1 |

Q-lite reduced reminder noise but took more turns and did not improve source
accuracy or protocol completion. Under the preregistered decision rule, that is
not a clear efficiency win and does not justify preferring Q-lite.

This result supersedes any simple reading of the raw 0/6 versus 0/6 totals. It
does not supersede the raw files; the validity failure and valid subset are both
reported explicitly.

## Frozen design

- Model: `claude-sonnet-5`.
- Tasks: `zod-5917` and `zod-5937`.
- Three repeats per task and arm.
- `--no-repro`: future fix-test contents were absent from agent checkouts and
  installed only in separate scorers after generation.
- Network and web tools denied; authentic history sealed at each pre-fix commit.
- Q received the task-relative episode, 6–7 broad obligations, and the probe's
  baseline/validation pair (8–9 obligations total).
- Q-lite received the same episode and probe plus exactly one post-edit compact
  regression command (3 obligations total).
- Source accuracy was primary; protocol resolution, turns, and reminders were
  secondary.

The design and decision rule were frozen before the runs in
`2026-08-24-zod-q-lite-preregistration.md`.

## Validity audit

All 12 sessions were operationally valid: authentication worked, sealed
checkouts were created, probes executed, scorer tests ran, probe artifacts were
untouched, and no infrastructure failure was recorded.

Operational validity was not enough. After scoring, the authentic source fix
was applied to each pre-fix checkout while retaining the exact old validation
files seen by the agents:

- `zod-5917`: the correct source passed all 10 full-controller files (252/252)
  and all Q-lite files (220/220). Its six Q/R rows remain valid.
- `zod-5937`: the correct source failed the Q-lite command in `partial.test.ts`
  and `to-json-schema.test.ts`. Those old expectations assert that missing catch
  inputs remain required, while the issue's correct fix deliberately restores
  catch fallback materialization and updates those expectations. Both Q and
  Q-lite required the incompatible files to pass, so all six rows are invalid
  for efficacy.

The benchmark now records this known incompatibility and refuses future
issue-only X/Q/R runs for `zod-5937` instead of silently repeating the invalid
contract.

## What the valid failures teach us

All six valid `zod-5917` agents reproduced the bug, turned the narrow probe
green, preserved existing tests, and still chose the wrong abstraction. Five
edited only core `schemas.ts`; one edited only classic `schemas.ts`. Their
explanations converged on a plausible local diagnosis: optionality is lost when
preprocess is represented as `pipe(transform, schema)`. They then modified the
generic pipe or transform contract.

The held-out fix instead introduces a thin specialized preprocess subtype and
updates the classic/core/type/JSON-Schema surfaces together. The controller was
successful at making agents prove their chosen hypothesis, but it did not make
them generate and discriminate multiple architectural hypotheses. Running more
checks against existing behavior could not reveal new type and representation
contracts that the old suite did not contain.

## Product decision

- Do not enable Q-lite by default and do not claim an accuracy gain.
- Keep the three-receipt arm as experimental infrastructure; it is less noisy,
  but not demonstrably more efficient or accurate.
- Never use a whole pre-fix suite as an immutable regression contract until the
  authentic fix has been checked against that exact suite. Intended semantic
  changes can make old expectations anti-ground-truth.
- Stop optimizing reminder timing. The current bottleneck is hypothesis search
  and discrimination, not evidence delivery.

The next experiment should be a **contrastive hypothesis tournament**:

1. require two materially different candidate mechanisms before the first edit;
2. generate one small discriminator that can make at least one candidate lose;
3. use issue/episode-derived positive and negative controls rather than entire
   old test files;
4. validate every prescribed control against both the authentic pre-fix and
   authentic fix in the scorer harness without exposing the fix to the agent;
5. only then run a repeated sealed comparison.

For `zod-5937`, a useful contrast is target catch fallback materialization versus
the neighboring rule that an outer optional wrapper still returns `undefined`
for absent input. For `zod-5917`, the discriminator must test whether the change
belongs to a specialized preprocess contract rather than globally weakening
generic pipe/transform optionality.
